title: MetaVLA: Unified Meta Co-Training for Efficient Embodied Adaptation
claim: One unified co-trained model beats per-task baselines, reaching higher accuracy with far fewer training steps and faster convergence.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: scatter, one-vs-many diagram, curves; handwritten annotations
description: Three side-by-side panels, each with a bold caption underneath. Panel (a) is a scatter plot of LIBERO success rate against total training steps. OpenVLA (blue circle) sits far right at about 240K steps. SFT-4LIBERO (orange square) is at 75K steps. MetaVLA (green triangle) is at 75K steps and the highest success rate. Black arrows and handwritten annotations mark '4.4% Higher Success Rate' and '68.75% Fewer Training Steps'. Panel (b) is a diagram on a split background, red on the left and green on the right. On the left, four separate models each connect to one LIBERO suite, with red crosses and '0 Success Rate' labels on the cross-task links. On the right, all four suites feed one 'Co-Trained Model' through green lines. The labels are 'One-for-Each: OpenVLA' and 'One-for-All: MetaVLA'. Panel (c) is a training-accuracy curve over iterations. The MetaVLA curve rises quickly to about 0.95. The baseline curve stays flat near 0.25.
caption: Three Key Merits of MetaVLA Compared to Baseline Approaches.
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models show promise in embodied reasoning, yet remain far from true generalists-they often require task-specific fine-tuning, incur high compute costs, and generalize poorly to unseen tasks. We propose MetaVLA, a unified, backbone-agnostic post-training framework for efficient and scalable alignment. MetaVLA introduces Context-Aware Meta Co-Training, which consolidates diverse target tasks into a single fine-tuning stage while leveraging structurally diverse auxiliary tasks to improve in-domain generalization. Unlike naive multi-task SFT, MetaVLA integrates a lightweight meta-learning mechanism-derived from Attentive Neural Processes-to enable rapid adaptation from diverse contexts with minimal architectural change or inference overhead. On the LIBERO benchmark, MetaVLA with six auxiliary tasks outperforms OpenVLA by up to 8.0% on long-horizon tasks, reduces training steps from 240K to 75K, and cuts GPU time by ~76%. These results show that scalable, low-resource post-training is achievable-paving the way toward general-purpose embodied agents. Code will be available.
